- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is falling, model often underestimates further drop; add 1–2% buffer below true low.
- Model frequently underestimates long-term mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if sentiment is mixed or neutral, apply slight upward bias toward historical mean of last 10–15 days.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is rising, model often overfits short-term momentum; reduce forecast slope or add smoothing factor to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33–0.67), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >10% over 10 days), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% per 3-day window if sentiment supports it.
- If sentiment is uniformly low (≤0.2) and price is flat or declining, model often overcorrects downward; add 0.5–1% upward bias to avoid premature bottoming.
